newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds at highs on review, CPI waits.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds at highs on review, CPI waits.

text.p: *Australian bonds finish down but are bouyed in late trade, notably at short end, by release of the mid-year budget review.
*Market waiting on U.S. employment cost index later today and local December quarter CPI data on Wednesday.
Australian bonds ended weaker, but near their highs for the day, after the government's release of its mid-year budget review proved a mixed bag for debt markets.
The review deflected the attention from upcoming U.S. wage inflation data later today and local CPI figures on Wednesday.
The review left the government's GDP forecast for 1996/97 (July-June) unchanged at 3.5 percent, lowered the inflation forecasts and lifted the unemployment rate forecast.
Initially bonds showed little reaction, moving both higher and then lower, before some late buying strengthened into the close, most notably into the short end.

"I think most people had accepted that the government was probably going to revise back its inflation forecasts, the only surprise was how much they revised them back perhaps," UBS Australia chief economist Stephen Roberts said.
"Offsetting that is a surprise on the other side -- they really haven't revised down their growth forecasts," he said.
The government announced a larger than expected underlying budget deficit of A$8.49 billion for 1996/97 from the forecast of A$5.65 billion in the August budget, suggesting increased bond issuance.

"It's going to add a few billion dollars worth of bonds to the issuing task in the next few years, but it's got to be remembered that there's an expanding supply of pension fund assets occuring at the same time," Merrill Lynch Australia chief economist Nigel Douglas said.
"So it may not have a big impact overall, but I think the initial expectations effect may be marginally negative," he said.
Markets are now waiting on the release of the U.S. December quarter ECI later today, as it is expected to determine market sentiment going into next week's FOMC meeting.

Market expectations of favourable local inflation data on Wednesday were bolstered by the downward revisions to inflation in the mid year review. Forecasts centre on a CPI of 1.6 percent over the last year and an annual underlying rate of 2.1 percent.

Spreads finished mixed, but improve on their weaker opening levels as bonds strengthen into the close. With short end supported by lower inflation and higher unemployment forecasts, curves reverse some of their recent steepening.
